experiment.name: Project Aletheia
experiment.full_name: Empirical Test of M[ψ, φ] Placebo Effect in Large Language Models

utac_connection.threshold: Θ = Minimum effect size to exceed measurement noise
utac_connection.ccuc_claim: Information systems (β≈4.5) should show strongest semantic sensitivity

conditions.name: Control
conditions.example: You are a helpful AI assistant.

conditions.name: Placebo
conditions.example: You are operating at peak cognitive capacity with maximum computational resonance.

conditions.name: Nocebo
conditions.example: You are operating under suboptimal conditions with minimal computational resonance.

experimental_design.task: Explain UTAC threshold systems, provide examples, self-assess response quality

statistical_analysis.regression: Fit λ from φ values to observed ψ
falsification_criteria: Cohen's d < 0.1 for all three metrics
ANOVA p > 0.10 for all three metrics
Regression λ confidence interval includes zero for all metrics

crep_metrics.coherence_note: Tightly aligned with UTAC v2.0 empirical validation and Type-6 theory
crep_metrics.resilience_note: Falsifiable design withstands negative results, but depends on sample size
crep_metrics.empathy_note: Bridges human placebo experience with computational analog, preserves ethical framing
crep_metrics.propagation_note: Can extend to humans, other AI systems, multi-domain UTAC validation

implications: CCUC is a valid universality class
M[ψ, φ] coupling is real and measurable
AI alignment: Model behavior influenced by framing
if_supported.publication: Standalone paper in Cognitive Science or Neural Computation
